Venaani calls for emergency FMD relief f.final_text: The Ministry of Finance acknowledges the concerns raised regarding Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) relief and the financial obligations of affected farmers. It is important to clarify that the collection of revenue by the Namibia Revenue Agency (Namra) is a statutory requirement mandated by law to ensure the sustainability of public services. The Ministry does not have the unilateral authority to waive these obligations without adherence to established legislative frameworks. However, the Ministry is actively engaging with relevant authorities to assess the specific impact of the FMD outbreak on the agricultural sector. We are reviewing potential mechanisms within the existing legal framework to support affected businesses and farmers during this challenging period. The government remains committed to balancing fiscal responsibility with the welfare of its citizens. We assure the public that the matter is being addressed with due diligence, and any decisions regarding temporary relief or support measures will be communicated through official channels in strict compliance with the law.

IPC unhappy about TransNamib executives’.final_text: The Ministry of Works and Transport acknowledges the concerns raised regarding the status of disciplinary hearings involving Trans Namib executives. We note the criticism concerning the perceived disparity in the pace of administrative processes between senior and junior staff. The Ministry is committed to upholding the highest standards of accountability and fairness within all its entities. We wish to clarify that the relevant authorities are actively engaged in addressing the matter in accordance with established legal frameworks and internal disciplinary procedures. Any delays are being managed to ensure due process is strictly adhered to, without compromising the integrity of the investigation. The Ministry remains dedicated to resolving these issues promptly and transparently. We assure the public that all necessary steps are being taken to ensure that justice is served and that the operations of Trans Namib continue to be governed by principles of good governance and professional conduct.

Minister Indileni Daniel launches probe.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
Minister Indileni Daniel launches probe.final_text: The Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism acknowledges the recent media reports concerning the operational oversight of Nam Water (NWR). We note that parliamentary inquiries regarding NWR’s financial standing have been raised by political parties, and we respect the legitimate role of the National Assembly in holding state institutions accountable. It is important to clarify that any investigative process is conducted with strict adherence to legal protocols to ensure the integrity and independence of the findings. The Ministry does not intervene in the internal financial operations of autonomous entities but supports transparent governance. Relevant authorities are currently addressing the matter through established channels. The Ministry remains committed to environmental stewardship and public accountability. We assure the Namibian public that all actions taken are in the best interest of national resource management and institutional integrity. Further updates will be provided through official government communication channels as the process progresses.
